As a water treatment professional/plumber for over 20 years I can tell you the smell comes from sulphur dioxide, not iron. You may or may not have iron, either way lots of ways available to eliminate the problem.

Many types of mixed media. high end catalytic softening resins etc can do the job. Old school is green sand filter. Many unscrupulous H20 treatment dealers will charge you 1, 2, 3, thousand bucks. Know that if you have a salesman come to your house your probably going to over pay. They are like juiced car salesmen for the most part and will pressure you into a bad decision.

Good news is aim small miss small. A double big blue canister setup 4 inch by 20 inch should be your starting point. You can get one for under 200 bucks, the canisters can handle a wide range of filters 1 micron then a solid block carbon is my choice. From there if your handy plumb it in right where the water enters the house. No need to filter all the water from the well. Very important to get 4 inch not the cheap 2.5 as the bigger ones allow for more contact time. This setup will remove cysts, micro organisms and other Mc nasties that may or may not be in your water. Also make sure the ports on the big blue are 1 inch not 3/4 (you will thank me later.)

This may or may not completely solve the problem of the smell and if you add media tanks, softeners, R O's after this it will only enhance their performance.

Many times iron is misdiagnosed as simple sand that is so fine it presents as iron. The 20 inch canisters eliminate this as well and depending on the feed water quality you may still have to change these filters every six months. Make sure and clean the canisters well before putting in the new filters. IMHO thats the best place to start, then go from there. Peace niggas.
